title: Writing / Glossary / Words to avoid
slide_intent: Replace internal shorthand with audience-facing language so people do not need organizational knowledge to understand the product.
strategic_value: The distinction can help Duolingo describe its learning experience in terms meaningful to learners.
demonstration: Three rows identify users, challenges and tree as terms to avoid externally and give learner-facing alternatives.
practical_value: Check whether a word is internal shorthand before using it in public copy.

content_islands.name: Guidance column
content_islands.spec: Place Words to Avoid and the internal-versus-external scope note at left.

content_islands.name: Worked examples
content_islands.spec: Pair each discouraged term with its replacement or explanation at right, keeping the internal-use exception with users.

reference_purposes.Application: Three term substitutions demonstrate public-facing vocabulary.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The guide reserves users and tree for internal contexts, prefers learners externally, and uses exercises instead of challenges.

ingredient.name: Audience-facing terminology
ingredient.role: Remove organizational shorthand from public explanations.
ingredient.application: Use learners externally, exercises instead of challenges, and course-progress wording instead of tree.
ingredient.scope: Historical official guidelines from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot; this records the displayed guidance, not current Duolingo product behavior. Internal expressions such as user testing remain permitted; this is not a ban across all company writing.
